content.comment_body: Quick question: Can you set up an alphanumeric password directly on the [product_name] text display device, rather than using a button combination? I'm referring to entering a name, number, or similar.

Are you asking about the [article_no] and the [product_name] text display extension? In that case, you can assign a password for switching to administrator mode. The password can include letters or numbers. However, you cannot lock the complete display with a password.
[product_name] with [article_no] and standard text display, not the extended one.
From the manual dated 11/2009. You can download it here: [url] Edit: For users who prefer Spanish documentation, here's an alternative link: [url]

After reviewing the manual, it appears the text display cannot be fully locked with a password. However, you can protect the program on the [product_name] and the stop/start function via the display with a password of up to 10 characters. Uppercase letters are supported.
You're right, and I believe these security features are sufficient for this type of control unit.

Thank you [user_name] for investigating this. I wasn't aware such protection was possible. I've already installed the device for a customer, who appreciated using button combinations to block certain functions. P.S. Thanks for sharing the Spanish manual; it was a thoughtful gesture, although I'm English working in Spain for a [company_name] solution partner. I still appreciate your help.
Hello [user_name], thanks for your feedback and rating.

Hi, additional password features can be programmed. For instance, an example of a 3-level password is available on the [product_name] website. Go to the [product_name] site, and it's listed at the end. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are exploring the capabilities of password protection on the [product_name] text display device. While some password security is available—such as protecting certain functions and administrator access—the device itself cannot be entirely locked using a password. Users have noted the limitation and have adapted by using available security methods, but there is an evident need for more comprehensive access control options to better meet end-user security requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the text display to support robust password protection using alphanumeric credentials, aiming for an easy way to restrict or lock device access beyond current function-specific protection. The desired feature is a straightforward password mechanism, rather than relying on button combinations.
